description: Fence highlighting waits until a block comes near the view. The conversation {{ID}} is a medium /debug/loremipsum conversation: every agent turn carries a code fence. "The blocks" are the ".message-agent pre > code" elements, in document order. 1. Navigate to /c/{{ID}}. 2. The first element with data-testid "message" should be visible (allow 30s). 3. Eval (() => { const b = document.querySelectorAll('.message-agent pre > code'); return b.length > 0 && b[b.length - 1].querySelector('.shelley-code-token') !== null; })() until it returns true (allow 30s): the page loads pinned to the bottom, so the newest fence highlights. This wait is the barrier that makes the next checks meaningful: eager highlighting would have tokenized every block by now. 4. Eval document.querySelectorAll('.message-agent pre > code').length: it must be exactly "50". 5. Eval document.querySelector('.message-agent pre > code').querySelectorAll('.shelley-code-token').length: exactly "0" (the first fence, far above the fold, is still plain text). 6. Eval document.querySelectorAll('.shelley-code-token').length < 200: true (only the few blocks on screen are tokenized; each fence is about 13 tokens, so 50 eager blocks would be about 650). 7. Scroll the first block into the scrollport, disarming auto-follow first (without the wheel event its pin snaps the view back to the bottom), in exactly this eval: (() => { document.querySelector('.messages-container').dispatchEvent(new WheelEvent('wheel', { deltaY: -200, bubbles: true })); document.querySelector('.message-agent pre > code').scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' }); return 'scrolled'; })(), expecting "scrolled". 8. Eval document.querySelector('.message-agent pre > code').querySelector('.shelley-code-token') !== null until it returns true (allow 30s): scrolling it in highlights it.
